quote: we built that solar estimate for your home, but just haven't been able to get that out to you yet
stewart_read: Rep frames the call as pure logistics/reschedule without reinforcing why the customer wanted solar in the first place, missing a chance to re-anchor interest before scheduling.
alternative_hypothesis: Strategic: since the customer was already warm and immediately moved to scheduling, re-litigating interest may have been unnecessary friction.
coaching_implication: Even a 10-second interest reaffirmation ('what got you looking at solar again?') would give the closer something to work with — right now the handoff has zero interest context.

quote: Yeah. They just texted me a little bit ago. I didn't know if you're find out.
stewart_read: Customer references a prior design/text and the rep does not probe what was in it, what company built it, or what the customer thought of it.
alternative_hypothesis: Reactive: rep is likely following an internal 'reschedule' script for previously-designed leads where this context is assumed already on file.
coaching_implication: A quick probe ('did you get a chance to look at the numbers?') could surface objections before the appointment and give the closer a head start.

quote: Are you gonna be around tomorrow?
stewart_read: Rep opens scheduling with a vague availability question instead of proposing one concrete slot, ceding control of the pace of the call.
alternative_hypothesis: Reactive failure — a single anchored offer ('Does 5 PM tomorrow work?') would have been faster.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to lead with one specific day/time offer rather than open questions when scheduling.

quote: Wednesday. Yeah. We could do Wednesday evening. We could also do 09:00
stewart_read: Second instance of the same non-anchoring pattern — rep again stacks multiple options across two different days instead of narrowing to one.
alternative_hypothesis: Reactive; no strategic upside to offering that many options simultaneously.
coaching_implication: This is the second occurrence of the pattern in the same call — a repeat sign the rep defaults to open-menu scheduling rather than a single confident anchor.

stewart_read: Time is locked but button_up is incomplete — no hour-block statement, no explicit 'is that fair' handshake, and no direct confirmation that the spouse ('she') will be present.
coaching_implication: Given the customer referenced his wife's schedule twice, the rep should have explicitly confirmed she'd be on the appointment rather than assuming from the customer's own scheduling check.

quote: I got a meeting at 04:30 in Indian Hill, and I won't be back here till six.
stewart_read: Customer references his wife's schedule ('she's got a softball thing') suggesting she is a co-decider, but rep never explicitly confirms she'll be on the call/appointment.
alternative_hypothesis: Strategic: rep may be relying on the customer to coordinate with his wife implicitly since he was checking 'her schedule' throughout.
coaching_implication: Should have asked directly: 'Will your wife be able to join us at 5?' to lock a two-person appointment per protocols.spouse_decision.
